claims.source: Project Blue Book Special Report No. 14 provenance; contemporaneous Air Force records
claims.text: Battelle's classified US Air Force contract to analyse Project Blue Book's UFO data was designated Project Stork, and its statistical study was published as Special Report No. 14 in 1955.

claims.source: CUFON transcription of the Pentacle Memorandum
claims.text: The 9 January 1953 Cross memorandum was written under Project Stork and addressed to Miles E. Goll at Wright-Patterson AFB.

claims.source: Project Stork status reports, First (25 April 1952) and Fifth (10 September 1952), transcribed from NARA holdings
claims.text: The contract is identified: from the Fifth Status Report onward the heading reads 'on CONTRACT AF-19741, PPS-100'. The First Status Report of 25 April 1952 'describes progress on Project Stork PPS-100, from its inception on March 31, 1952 through April 25, 1952'.

claims.source: Project Stork, First Status Report, 25 April 1952
claims.text: The First Status Report lists the contract requirements: '1. Provide a panel of consultants, 2. Assist in improving interrogation forms, 3. Analyze existing sighting reports, 4. Subscribe to a clipping service, as directed, and 5. Apprise the Sponsor monthly of all work done on PPS-100.'

claims.source: Project Stork status reports, transcribed from NARA holdings, with the transcriber's scope note
claims.text: Seven status reports are publicly available, totalling 107 pages, dated 25 April, 6 June, 7 July, 11 August, 10 September, 10 October and 10 November 1952. All are addressed 'to AIR TECHNICAL INTELLIGENCE CENTER, WRIGHT-PATTERSON AIR FORCE BASE'. The set is known to be incomplete: the holding archive's own scope note records that 'these (107) pages are not the total paper generated by Project Stork. Internal references to other documents exist in this text, including further Status Reports. None of these is in the custody of the NARA.'

claims.source: Project Stork status reports, Third Status Report, 7 July 1952, and the redaction pattern across the set
claims.text: In most released copies the contractor's name is crossed out and supplied by a handwritten annotation reading '{Battelle}'. The Third Status Report of 7 July 1952 is the only one where it is typed rather than struck out: 'by BATTELLE MEMORIAL INSTITUTE'. That single untouched line is how the attribution survives at all.

claims.source: Project Blue Book Special Report No. 14, 5 May 1955, full-text search of the scan; read against the Project Stork status reports
claims.text: Special Report No. 14 does not name its contractor on its own face. A full-text search of the report returns no occurrence of Battelle, Columbus, Stork, contractor, 'prepared by' or 19741. The Battelle and Stork attribution rests entirely on the status reports and the surrounding record: the analytical work was contracted out and the published product did not say so.

claims.source: Project Stork file, ATIC record of 8 January 1952 and the Hynek report of 6 August 1952, transcribed from NARA holdings
claims.text: The same file contains an ATIC record of 8 January 1952, 'AUTH: CO, ATIC / BY: E. J. Ruppelt, 1st Lt. USAF', recording that Ruppelt and Col. Kirkland conferred with the contractor on 26 December 1951 about Project Grudge, annotated by hand 'Background - How Special Rept No. 14 came into being'. It also contains a 'SPECIAL REPORT on CONFERENCES WITH ASTRONOMERS ON UNIDENTIFIED AERIAL OBJECTS to AIR TECHNICAL INTELLIGENCE CENTER WRIGHT-PATTERSON AIR FORCE BASE by J. Allen Hynek, August 6, 1952'.

desc: Project Stork was the Air Force's contracted analytical arm for its own UFO investigation. Battelle Memorial Institute, in Columbus, Ohio, held the contract and performed the statistical work on Blue Book's case files that became Special Report No. 14. Stork is the reason a private applied-science institute, not the Air Force, controlled the analytical methodology by which UFO reports were classified as identified or unidentified for the entire Blue Book era. It is also the contract vehicle under which H. C. Cross wrote the Pentacle Memorandum on 9 January 1953 proposing covertly scheduled aerial activity in high-report areas - a proposal made by the contractor to the customer, in writing, on a project the public was told was a scientific investigation. Project Stork is the earliest clean instance of the mechanism this domain exists to document: the government's analytical judgement on anomalous phenomena being formed inside a private nonprofit whose records were never federal records.

timeline.label: Battelle contracted for Project Stork
timeline.text: The Air Force outsources the statistical analysis of Project Blue Book's case files to Battelle Memorial Institute in Columbus, Ohio, under the codename Project Stork.

timeline.label: Project Stork begins
timeline.text: Work begins on Project Stork, designation PPS-100, later carried as contract AF-19741, for the Air Technical Intelligence Center. The first status report of 25 April 1952 describes progress 'from its inception on March 31, 1952'. Seven status reports survive, totalling 107 pages, and the transcribing archive records that further reports referenced in the text are not in NARA custody.
